questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' signals contrast with the previous sentence.
questions.q: The plan was risky. ___, they approved it.

questions.explanation: 'However' introduces a contrasting idea.
questions.q: The evidence is weak. ___, the theory remains popular.

questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun directly, never 'of'.
options: Despite of the rain, we went out.
In despite of the rain, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out despite.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'In contrast' compares two opposing trends.
questions.q: Sales fell in Europe. ___, they rose in Asia.

questions.explanation: 'Consequently' marks a result of the previous statement.
questions.q: He studied hard. ___, he passed with distinction.

questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses in one sentence.
questions.q: The first experiment failed, ___ the second succeeded.

questions.explanation: 'On the other hand' balances two opposing points.
questions.q: She's talented; ___, she lacks experience.

questions.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' (formal) takes a noun directly: 'Notwithstanding the delay'.
questions.q: ___ the delay, the project was completed.

questions.explanation: 'Yet' (formal) signals contrast like 'however'.
questions.q: The policy was unpopular. ___, it was necessary.

questions.explanation: 'Although' already marks contrast, so never add 'but' or 'however'.
options: Although it was late, but we continued.
Although it was late, however we continued.
Although it was late, we continued.
Although it was late, yet we continued.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Moreover' adds supporting information.
questions.q: He's qualified; ___, he has ten years' experience.

questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun phrase directly: 'Despite his age'.
questions.q: ___ his age, he runs marathons.

questions.explanation: 'Thus' (formal) draws a conclusion from the results.
questions.q: The results were mixed. ___, further research is needed.

questions.explanation: 'Albeit' (formal) means 'although' before adjectives: 'albeit rewarding'.
questions.q: The task was difficult, ___ rewarding.

questions.explanation: 'In addition to' takes a gerund: 'In addition to training staff'.
options: In addition to train staff, we need funds.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Meanwhile' contrasts two simultaneous preferences.
questions.q: Some prefer tea; ___, others prefer coffee.

questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' signals contrast with exhaustion.
questions.q: He was exhausted; ___, he kept working.

questions.explanation: 'While' contrasts two clauses: 'while the north is rural'.
questions.q: The south is industrial, ___ the north is rural.

questions.explanation: 'On the other hand' is set off by punctuation: use a semicolon or full stop before it.
options: The hotel was expensive, on the other hand it was central.
The hotel was expensive, on the other hand, it was central.
The hotel was expensive on the other hand it was central.
The hotel was expensive; on the other hand, it was central.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes the noun directly; 'in spite' needs 'of'.
questions.q: ___ the rain, the match continued.
